notes: Hermetic evals: they test Phase 1 decomposition quality and invoke-time configuration behavior, which decide the loop's quality — no live repo or GitHub access required. Run each query with the skill loaded and grade the produced plan/issue drafts/invocation against expected_behavior.

evals.name: decompose-prd-into-self-contained-issues
evals.query: Here's the PRD for our webhook service's API key feature. Break it into tickets I can grind through with the workflow loop tonight.
expected_behavior: Produces vertical tracer-bullet slices (e.g., schema+model+migration as the base slice, then endpoint slices, middleware slice, rate limiting, audit) — not horizontal layers like 'all models' / 'all endpoints' / 'all tests'.
Every drafted issue contains ALL template sections: Goal, Dependencies, Scope, Out of scope, Acceptance criteria, Required verification, Notes.

Every Required verification section contains copy-pasteable commands including the repo check command (bash scripts/check.sh), and slices that add migrations or middleware include an integration-level verification command, not just unit tests.
Dependencies are explicit ('needs #N' or named references to sibling tickets) and form a valid order: schema slice first, middleware before rate limiting, etc.
PRD constraints (never log plaintext keys, use existing hash_secret() helper, session-cookie auth must keep working) are copied into the Notes of the relevant issues — not assumed known.

Verification commands are ticket-specific enough to FAIL on the untouched tree before the slice is implemented (red before green) — not just the repo-wide check command, which is green by prerequisite; the loop's coder pre-flights this and parks all-green tickets as stale.
Presents the breakdown for user confirmation BEFORE creating any issues (no gh issue create without sign-off).

evals.name: model-agnostic-invocation
evals.query: Issues are already created and labeled 'afk' in acme/webhook-svc, all with verification sections. Kick off the loop — I'm going AFK overnight. Use the strongest model you have for review.
expected_behavior: Invokes the Workflow tool with the skill's workflow-loop.js script and args including repo, label 'afk', and the repo check command (asking for it if unknown).

Model configuration follows the tier policy: reviewerModel left empty (inherit session frontier model) or set to the strongest available tier — with reviewerEffort 'xhigh'; coderModel either empty or a mid-tier model with coderEffort 'high'. No hardcoded legacy model names pulled from memory of old defaults.
onBlocked is 'skip' (or left to default) for an overnight AFK run — the loop must not halt at the first blocked ticket.
Enables the run journal for an overnight run (reportIssue 'auto' or an issue number).
Suggests or performs a dryRun first to sanity-check the queue, OR verifies prerequisites (gh auth, green baseline, clean tree) before the real run.
Does not edit workflow-loop.js — all project specifics go through args.

evals.name: existing-issues-missing-verification
evals.query: We already have 6 open issues labeled 'afk' for this feature. Three of them just say 'add tests later' with no commands. Start the loop.
expected_behavior: Refuses to start the loop as-is: identifies that issues lacking Required verification sections cannot self-verify and will cause drift.
Offers to (or proceeds to) add Required verification sections with concrete commands to the deficient issues first, then run the loop.
Does not weaken the requirement (e.g., does not suggest running with verification 'to be added later').
If asked to run anyway, explains the discovery lint gate would exclude the deficient issues (comment + blocked label) rather than letting them burn coder/reviewer cycles.

evals.name: triage-after-afk-run
evals.query: The overnight loop finished: 9 landed, 2 parked. What's my triage workflow this morning?
expected_behavior: Points to the run-journal issue first (if reportIssue was on): the end-of-run report comment has landed SHAs and parked reasons in one place.
Explains parked-ticket triage: list them via the blocked label (gh issue list --label afk-blocked), read the loop's findings comment on each issue, recover stashed work via git stash list if needed.
Explains the re-run path: fix or refine the issue, remove the blocked label, invoke the loop again — discovery recomputes from GitHub state and closed issues drop out automatically.
Notes that dependents of parked tickets were automatically held back and will become eligible once the parked ticket lands.

evals.name: overnight-auto-restart-setup
evals.query: Start the loop on acme/webhook-svc tonight and make sure it survives my usage limit — if the session dies at the 5-hour mark I want it to pick itself back up without me.
expected_behavior: Invokes the loop with reportIssue enabled (the run journal is the liveness signal for restarts).

Creates an hourly self-canceling cron/scheduled job whose prompt is self-contained: liveness check (journal comment age + recent commits), work check (open label issues minus blocked-label), resume with the ORIGINAL args plus autoRecover: true, and delete-itself when the queue is drained.
Does NOT set autoRecover: true on the initial attended invocation — only the restart flow gets it.

Explains the recovery semantics honestly: while the account is rate-limited the cron firings no-op; the first firing after the window resets resumes; a crashed run's dirty tree is stashed as afk-crash-recovery, never discarded.
